extracted.intended_audience: shippers, carriers, manufacturers, and regulators of Class 7 (radioactive) materials; radiography firms and other industry users of radioactive devices; hazardous materials compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Federal rulemaking discussion and final-rule requirements for packaging, labeling, marking, classification, and air/ground transport of Class 7 (radioactive) materials under the HMR, aligned with IAEA TS-R-1 where adopted. Covers overpack labeling, TI/CSI use, LSA/SCO definitions and transport (including unpackaged), UF6 packaging, and air-transport (Type C/LDM) criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: International marking for excepted small instruments/articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Excepted packages of instruments and articles containing small quantities of radioactive material must still have the “RADIOACTIVE” marking if they are to be transported under the IAEA Regulations in TS-R-1, the ICAO Technical Instructions, or the IMDG Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although commenters noted limited safety benefit vs. manufacturer cost for marking very small items, the rule acknowledges international consistency: if shipped under the listed international instruments the marking is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overpack label category determination (final rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The category of the overpack is to be determined, by the procedure described in §172.403(b) for packages, using the maximum dose rate on the surface of the overpack, and the transport index (TI) for the overpack is to be determined by one of the methods prescribed in §172.403(h)(3) for a non-rigid overpack, or in §172.403(h)(4) for a rigid overpack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency removed the proposed restriction that would have required the overpack to 'satisfy the packaging requirements for the package type appropriate for the totality of its contents' (which could have forced use of sturdier/Type B packagings). The change avoids forcing use of overly restrictive overpacks and addresses commenter concerns about unintended placarding/operational burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label category impacts placarding and carrier qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The label category assigned to an overpack or package (e.g., Yellow-III) can trigger placarding requirements and associated carrier obligations, such as use of placarded vehicles, drivers holding Commercial Driver's Licenses (CDLs), and Registered Shipper status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters argued that changes increasing Yellow-III labeling could impose significant costs and operational impacts (placarding, CDL, registered shipper) without added safety and could discourage use of overpacks, possibly increasing overall radiation exposure through more handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: SI units required with optional customary units in parentheses
rubrics_metrics.description: SI units must be used on markings and shipping papers; customary units may continue to be used only if they are placed within parentheses after the required SI units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule adds the requirement that customary units, if used, be enclosed in parentheses (the present regulations allowed customary units after SI units but did not require parentheses). This facilitates international harmonization while preserving familiarity for carriers and responders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticality Safety Index (CSI) numeric format and source
rubrics_metrics.description: The CSI for packages containing fissile material is determined in accordance with the instructions provided in 10 CFR 71.22, 71.23, and 71.59, and is a number rounded up to the nearest tenth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency inserted this clarification into the definition of CSI in §173.403 to specify the numerical format for guidance to shippers and carriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: FISSILE label and separation of TI (radiation) and CSI (criticality) hazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt use of a Fissile label and the Criticality Safety Index (CSI) to communicate the criticality hazard separately from the transport index (TI), which refers to external radiation hazard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency explains uncoupling TI and CSI improves clarity — CSI conveys criticality hazard information better than vague warnings. The proper shipping name also includes 'Radioactive material' for general radiation communication. Overloading labels with alarming or ambiguous language (e.g., 'Very Dangerous, Radioactive...') is discouraged as it may overwhelm responders and increase error risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: §175.702 cargo aircraft limits (FISSILE/CSI/TI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final changes in §175.702 included reference to a FISSILE label in §175.702(b), a restriction to a total CSI of 50 in §175.702(b), and the introduction of an upper limit of 200 TI for cargo aircraft only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No adoption of the ICAO/IAEA segregation scheme in this rulemaking; DOT notes the ICAO segregation table (allowing up to 200 TI) but did not adopt that scheme here and may consider the discrepancy in a future rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: LSA-I definition aligned with TS-R-1 (new activity threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt TS-R-1's new category of LSA-I: radioactive material, excluding non-excepted fissile material, in which the activity is distributed throughout and the estimated average specific activity does not exceed 30 times the activity concentration exemption values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previous LSA-I category (specific materials with average specific activity ≤10^-1 A2/g) is eliminated. Materials formerly listed (e.g., earth, concrete, rubble, mill tailings) may still be classified as LSA-I if they meet the new definition. The change standardizes with international community and is expected to reduce confusion over time; training is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization to transport unpackaged LSA-I and SCO-I (industrial packagings permitted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unpackaged LSA-I and SCO-I may be transported by means of qualified tank containers, freight containers and metal intermediate bulk containers as industrial packagings, types 2 and 3 (IP-2 and IP-3), subject to the requirements of §173.427.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unpackaged shipments (except certain ores) are allowed when conditions in §173.427(c) are met (no escape of contents or loss of shielding), and may require exclusive use. Where unpackaged transport is allowed, the carrier of an exclusive use shipment must survey and decontaminate the conveyance as necessary in accordance with §173.443(c) prior to unrestricted release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpackaged LSA-I and SCO-I subject to same transport controls as packaged material
rubrics_metrics.description: Unpackaged LSA-I and SCO-I are subject to the same transport controls as packaged LSA material and SCO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule added wording in §173.427(a)(4), (a)(6)(iii), and (a)(6)(vi) to clarify transport controls for unpackaged materials and to ensure comparable safety measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking requirement for exclusive-use LSA-I and SCO-I shipments
rubrics_metrics.description: For exclusive use shipments, the marking 'RADIOACTIVE LSA-I' or 'RADIOACTIVE SCO-I' is required (retained in final rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency retains these marking requirements because they serve the useful purpose of alerting emergency response personnel that Class 7 material is present, even at relatively low concentrations, and thus the marking is not made optional for domestic exclusive-use transports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and test guidance for 'distributed throughout' and 'essentially uniformly distributed'
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance consistent with NUREG-1608: For packages containing at least 0.2 m3 of LSA material, ten or more equal volumes no greater than 0.1 m3 each, of objects or materials that are 'distributed throughout,' should not vary by more than a factor of ten. For 'essentially uniformly distributed' the specific activity among similarly defined volumes should not vary by more than a factor of three. 'Estimated average specific activity' is the arithmetic average specific activity where ranges do not vary by more than the specified factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This guidance may be applied quantitatively or qualitatively where LSA materials contain radionuclides in quantities less than 1 A2; it assists shippers in applying the LSA-I definition practically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of 'contamination' definition (removal of ambiguous phrase)
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'Non-fixed (removable) radioactive contamination is not significant if it does not exceed the limits specified in §173.443' was removed as redundant/ambiguous; the definition of contamination designates a threshold value below which material is not subject to Class 7 transport regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The clarified definition aligns with radioactive material definitions and reduces ambiguity about when contamination triggers regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: UF6 packaging tests and design requirements (packagings >0.1 kg UF6)
rubrics_metrics.description: For packagings containing more than 0.1 kg of UF6, require the packaging to meet the 'normal conditions of transport' drop test, a minimum internal pressure test and the hypothetical accident condition thermal test (IAEA TS-R-1 paragraph 630).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also: prohibit the use of pressure relief devices for UF6 packagings (TS-R-1 paragraph 631) and provide designated packaging certification identification marks in accordance with TS-R-1 paragraph 828. DOT did not adopt ISO 7195 for domestic use because differences with ANSI N14.1 remained unresolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: UF6 evaluation exception for water in-leakage (Paragraph 677(b) conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under TS-R-1 Paragraph 677(b), UF6 packages may be evaluated without considering the in-leakage of water into the containment system if packages satisfy specified conditions: no contact between the valve and any other component under hypothetical accident tests, the valve remains leak-tight after the thermal test, and a high degree of quality control in manufacture/maintenance/repair with tests to demonstrate closure of each package before shipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is not considered relaxation of prior regulatory requirements but an enumeration of existing agency practices. Competent authority package design certificates are required for international shipments of UF6 under specified paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type C package thresholds and performance tests for air transport
rubrics_metrics.description: Type C package requirements apply to radionuclide packages for air transport containing total activity values above 3,000 A1 or 100,000 A2 (whichever is less) for special form material, or above 3,000 A2 for all other radioactive material. Type C performance tests are significantly more stringent than Type B: e.g., a 90-meter per second (m/s) impact test (vs. 9 m drop) and a 60-minute fire test (vs. 30-minute).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These stringent requirements aim to ensure packaging survival under severe aircraft accident conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low Dispersible Material (LDM) criteria for air transport
rubrics_metrics.description: LDM is a material exception allowing materials that would otherwise require a Type C package to be transported by aircraft in a Type B package if the material demonstrates limited dispersibility and leachability. Tests for LDM are a subset of Type C (including 90 m/s impact and 60-minute thermal test) with an added solubility test, must be performed on the material without packaging, and the LDM must have an external radiation level below 10 mSv/h (1 rem/hr) at 3 meters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific acceptance criteria for LDM performance: less than 100 A2 in gaseous or particulate form of <100 micrometer aerodynamic equivalent diameter and less than 100 A2 in solution. These criteria are intended to ensure safe continued transport in Type B packages aboard aircraft.
